findings.title: SPF exceeds the 10 DNS lookup limit

detection_methods.prior_justification: the count is computed from records we fetched ourselves, but include chains change often and a chain we could not finish walking returns inconclusive

evidence.label: TXT at bankrate.com

records: v=spf1 include:spf.protection.outlook.com include:email.prnewswire.com include:amazonses.com include:mailgun.org include:cisionone.cision.com ip4:149.72.161.134 ~all

evidence.control_rationale: a random-label probe in the same zone; without it a wildcard would make every lookup under this domain appear to succeed

record.raw: v=spf1 include:spf.protection.outlook.com include:email.prnewswire.com include:amazonses.com include:mailgun.org include:cisionone.cision.com ip4:149.72.161.134 ~all

problems: include loop: mailgun.org is already in the chain

evidence.label: independent re-query via 8.8.8.8

records: v=spf1 include:spf.protection.outlook.com include:email.prnewswire.com include:amazonses.com include:mailgun.org include:cisionone.cision.com ip4:149.72.161.134 ~all

evidence.control_rationale: the control for this re-query is the first resolver's answer, captured above

findings.description: Evaluating this SPF policy needs 12 DNS lookups, above the limit of 10 in RFC 7208 section 4.6.4. The chain is: bankrate.com (5) -> spf.protection.outlook.com (0) -> email.prnewswire.com (1) -> amazonses.com (0) -> mailgun.org (2) -> cisionone.cision.com (2) -> ab.sendgrid.net (0) -> _spf.mailgun.org (2) -> _spf.eu.mailgun.org (0) -> %{i}._ip.%{h}._ehlo.%{d}._spf.vali.email (0) -> _spf1.mailgun.org (0) -> _spf2.mailgun.org (0).
findings.impact: Receivers stop evaluating and return permerror, so SPF fails for this domain entirely. Legitimate mail can be rejected and forged mail is not caught.
findings.remediation: Reduce the chain below ten lookups. The usual fix is to replace include: terms for providers you no longer use, and to flatten a provider's ranges into ip4:/ip6: terms - those cost no lookups at all.

findings.title: DMARC uses relaxed alignment

detection_methods.prior_justification: the adkim= and aspf= tags are read directly, and default to relaxed

evidence.label: TXT at _dmarc.bankrate.com
evidence.control_rationale: a random-label probe in the same zone; without it a wildcard would make every lookup under this domain appear to succeed

evidence.label: independent re-query via 8.8.8.8
evidence.control_rationale: the control for this re-query is the first resolver's answer, captured above

findings.description: DMARC alignment is relaxed (adkim=r, aspf=r). Relaxed alignment accepts any subdomain of bankrate.com in the authenticated identifier.
findings.impact: Relaxed alignment is the default and is appropriate for most senders. It does mean that anyone able to publish records under a subdomain can pass DMARC for the parent.
findings.remediation: If every legitimate sender signs and sends as the exact domain, set adkim=s and aspf=s. If subdomains send mail, relaxed is the correct setting and no change is needed.

findings.title: No MTA-STS policy published

detection_methods.prior_justification: a definite TXT answer at _mta-sts with no v=STSv1 term is direct observation

evidence.label: TXT at _mta-sts.bankrate.com
evidence.control_rationale: a random-label probe in the same zone; without it a wildcard would make every lookup under this domain appear to succeed

evidence.label: independent re-query via 8.8.8.8
evidence.control_rationale: the control for this re-query is the first resolver's answer, captured above

findings.description: No MTA-STS policy record is published at _mta-sts.bankrate.com.
findings.impact: Without MTA-STS a sending server that cannot negotiate TLS will deliver mail in plaintext rather than refusing, so an attacker positioned on the network can strip encryption and read the message.
findings.remediation: Publish a TXT record at _mta-sts.bankrate.com of the form 'v=STSv1; id=<timestamp>', and serve the matching policy file at https://mta-sts.bankrate.com/.well-known/mta-sts.txt. Start the policy in mode: testing, then move to mode: enforce.

findings.title: No SMTP TLS reporting configured

detection_methods.prior_justification: a definite TXT answer at _smtp._tls with no v=TLSRPTv1 term is direct observation

evidence.label: TXT at _smtp._tls.bankrate.com
evidence.control_rationale: a random-label probe in the same zone; without it a wildcard would make every lookup under this domain appear to succeed

evidence.label: independent re-query via 8.8.8.8
evidence.control_rationale: the control for this re-query is the first resolver's answer, captured above

findings.description: No SMTP TLS reporting record is published at _smtp._tls.bankrate.com.
findings.impact: Nobody is told when a sending server fails to establish TLS to your mail servers, so a downgrade attack or a broken certificate goes unnoticed.
findings.remediation: Publish a TXT record at _smtp._tls.bankrate.com of the form 'v=TLSRPTv1; rua=mailto:tls-reports@bankrate.com'.
